Preliminary model robustness checks

Cumulative mortality and forest-community climate-niche change

What these checks answer

The current preliminary model remains the reference model. These checks ask whether its disturbance coefficients depend on:

  1. comparing different condition histories across life stages;
  2. retaining conditions that occupy only part of a plot;
  3. broad geographic differences among states;
  4. representing site water deficit as cumulative exposure while also including survey duration.

They also test life-stage differences directly on identical histories. They do not introduce a new severity definition or replace cumulative mortality.

Main findings

  • All 18 disturbance coefficients whose baseline 95% interval excluded zero retained the same direction across every applicable check.
  • All 18 remained below p = 0.05 with state effects, mean monthly CWD, and cumulative CWD without the separate survey-period term.
  • 16 of those 18 remained below p = 0.05 when conditions were required to occupy at least 80% of the plot.
  • On the smaller identical-history sample, 7 of the 10 supported life-stage coefficients remained below p = 0.05. Their loss of precision should not be read as proof of no effect.
  • 2 of the 15 joint life-stage tests were below p = 0.05. These tests identify sapling-adult differences that are larger than expected from sampling uncertainty under the model.
  • Even the state-effects models explain at most 1.06% of response variance. These remain weakly predictive, observational preliminary models.

Reproduction check

The robustness script refit the approved models before changing anything. The largest absolute coefficient difference was 4.718448e-16 and the largest standard-error difference was 4.857226e-17.

Does condition spatial support matter?

The current analysis requires a condition to occupy at least 30% of the plot. The 80% check retains histories whose condition remains at least 80% of the plot through every interval. This tests whether partial-plot conditions are driving the preliminary relationships.

Cumulative CWD and survey duration

Three formulations are compared in the stability figure:

  • the approved model with cumulative CWD and survey duration;
  • mean monthly CWD and survey duration;
  • cumulative CWD without a separate duration term.

The alternative formulations are diagnostics. Cumulative CWD remains the intended total-exposure predictor unless the collaborators choose otherwise.

Interpretation

These are observational preliminary models with very low explained variance. Coefficient direction and uncertainty are more informative here than p-values alone. A stable coefficient is not automatically causal, and an unstable coefficient identifies a modeling or sampling dependency that should be resolved before final inference.
